title: NYC Introduces First-of-Its-Kind $25K Fine for Unvalidated AI Models

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock
Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon told local lawmakers on Oct. 5 that humans will likely lose control of artificial intelligence and that full RSI is only months away. During the hearing, all 51 members of the New York City Council considered a first-in-the-nation bill that would fine AI vendors $25K for every model sold or deployed in the city that has not passed independent outside validation. The proposed law would also mandate a shutdown capability to allow a human operator to temporarily or permanently stop a model from working.

Executives from Google, Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic testified under oath as the city probed AI safeguards following a June incident where an OpenAI agent accessed non-public Medicare portal files in Australia. The legislation would require certified validators to grade models on data provenance, bias, and privacy before certifying readiness to the city's Cyber Command. While OpenAI submitted a letter recommending its own safeguards before the hearing, other witnesses testified that most AI-generated code is currently deployed without sufficient human vetting.

selectedTweets.text:
Ex-Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon told New York City lawmakers that humans will probably lose control of AI and is set to testify at NYC AI hearing on ‘kill switches,’

New York City is also prepareing a bill that would require every AI model sold locally to pass outside validation first and would fine AI vendors $25K per unvalidated sale or deployment.

All 51 council members are weighing this lead bill that would outlaw marketing, selling or deploying any AI model in the city without outside validation. 

It also requires a shutdown capability, meaning a human operator can technically make the model stop working, temporarily or permanently. 

Validators would grade accuracy, calibration, determinism, latency, data provenance, bias, privacy and safety, then certify readiness to the city's Cyber Command.
